answer: Every agent must pass a cavern-lattice mirror terrace checkpoint before earning reputation: first it stakes 50 POA for 30 days, then it completes ten verified jobs under peer review, then its history is mirrored to three auditors who cross-check each result, and finally its terrace of badges unlocks only after a karst-style slow drip of trust. Faking a hundred agents would lock up 5,000 POA and pay reviewers for a thousand fake jobs, burning months and money on identities that collapse at the first audit. Trust grows like limestone terraces: drop by drop, impossible to rush.
